Patellar aplasia/hypoplasia and microtia are defining features. Microcephaly alone does not establish neurologic dysfunction; airway disease frequency is unclear.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism disorder; encephalopathy and developmental impairment are common (>30%). Cardiac, hepatic and muscle injury vary across subtypes.
IgG4-mediated inflammation and fibrosis of bile ducts. Associated autoimmune pancreatitis is a separately diagnosed disease.

Inherited platelet-lineage disorder. Annotated thromboses and cerebral ischemia are separately diagnosed vascular complications; risks vary across subtypes.

Epithelial neoplasm originates in the vermiform appendix.
Gluconeogenesis defect; hepatic dysfunction/steatosis is common, with failure in 1/1 annotated. Neurologic injury is mainly described in severe cases, without reliable frequency.
Intrinsic disease of cardiac muscle cells; myocardium belongs to cardiovascular, not skeletal musculoskeletal tissue.
Defining intellectual and language impairment; strabismus and hypermetropia each affect 3/4. PFO and an aberrant artery alone do not establish cardiac dysfunction.
Dysplastic epithelial adenoma originates in the rectum.
Bone fragility disorder with increased bone mineral density. Common extra-skeletal damage is not established for this subtype.
Direct injury or dysfunction of an isolated peripheral nerve; underlying causes do not imply additional organ involvement.
Generalized dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; abnormal contractions alone do not establish skeletal muscle injury.
Acute substance intoxication with psychiatric and transient autonomic effects. Infarction, seizures and pulmonary or renal injury are minority complications.
Intellectual disability and skeletal malformations characterize the syndrome; VSD occurs in 30-79%. Dental caries is separate; ocular and hepatic anomalies are below 30%.
Defined by renal functional failure in advanced liver disease; both organs are intrinsic to the syndrome.
Neurodevelopmental and sacral abnormalities; strabismus 8/12, myopia 4/7, hearing loss 5/9. Aplasia cutis 5/10 omitted by cap; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
